title: Tanzanian Prawn Pilau
community: Zanzibar — the seafood pilau for major celebrations
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Prawn Pilau — basmati rice cooked in a rich prawn and coconut stock with Zanzibar spices, crowned with butter-sautéed prawns. The luxury seafood pilau of Zanzibar — the dish that celebrates the Indian Ocean's greatest gift.
longDesc: Prawn pilau is Zanzibar's most luxurious rice dish — the prawn shells make an intensely flavoured stock that cooks the rice, and the best prawns are saved for the final sauté and crowning of the dish.
ingredients: // Prawn Shell Stock: reserved shells, 4 cups water, 1 onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp salt
// Zanzibar Spices: 2 tsp cumin seeds, 6 cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon stick, 6 cloves
steps: Make prawn stock: simmer shells with water, onion, garlic, salt 20 minutes. Strain. Measure 5 cups.
Toast spices. Grind half. Keep half whole.
Cook onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, spices, tomatoes. Cook 8 minutes.
Add coconut milk and prawn stock. Bring to boil.
Add drained rice. Stir. Reduce heat. Cover tightly. Cook 18 minutes.
Sauté prawns in butter with garlic and salt — 3—4 minutes.
Crown pilau with sautéed prawns. Garnish with coriander.
chefTips: Prawn shell stock is the foundation — do not skip.
Prawn shells contain intense glutamate flavour.
Add prawns at the end — they cook in minutes.
commonMistakes: Adding raw prawns to the rice.
cookingScience: Prawn shells contain chitin-bound glutamate — amino acids that produce intense umami when extracted in hot water, giving the rice incomparable depth.
sustainabilityTips: Using prawn shells for stock — zero waste.
culturalNote: Prawn pilau is Zanzibar's most luxurious expression of the pilau tradition — taking the Indian Ocean's finest protein and the island's finest spices in the great rice dish of East Africa.
